paragraphs: As the vibrant green of your lawn transforms into unsightly brown patches, you may be dealing with a common issue in Baton Rouge, Louisiana—large patch disease. At Grow Green Weed Control, we understand the frustration that comes with watching your lawn lose its luster. In this blog post, we'll explore what large patch disease is, how it forms, and most importantly, how you can restore your lawn to its former glory with our expert treatment services.

Large patch disease, also known as brown patch, is a prevalent lawn fungus that targets warm-season grasses like Bermuda and St. Augustine—common choices for Baton Rouge lawns. It typically rears its head in the fall and spring when the weather conditions are favorable for fungal growth. The disease manifests as circular or irregular-shaped patches of brown or yellow grass, ranging from a few inches to several feet in diameter.

Large patch disease thrives in conditions of excess moisture, poor drainage, and cool temperatures. Baton Rouge's humid climate, combined with frequent rain, creates the perfect breeding ground for this fungus. The fungus, Rhizoctonia solani, attacks the grass at the crown and the roots, leading to weakened and discolored turf.

Understanding Large Patch Disease:

Large patch disease, also known as brown patch, is a prevalent lawn fungus that targets warm-season grasses like Bermuda and St. Augustine—common choices for Baton Rouge lawns. It typically rears its head in the fall and spring when the weather conditions are favorable for fungal growth. The disease manifests as circular or irregular-shaped patches of brown or yellow grass, ranging from a few inches to several feet in diameter.

How Large Patch Disease Forms:

Large patch disease thrives in conditions of excess moisture, poor drainage, and cool temperatures.
